note:
Measured 2026-07-28 from the first working reference and implementation across all eighteen Golden cases, then reviewed and committed. Regenerating these from a later run would defeat their purpose: a tolerance is an input to validation, not an output of it.

The oracle runs bfloat16 on CUDA and the port runs F32 on CPU, so these thresholds cover a dtype and a device difference as well as an implementation one. That is the comparison the contract asks for -- see docs/port-validation.md, 'Choosing the Oracle's dtype and Device' -- and not a weakness in them.

Talker probes gate on cosine similarity, not max-abs. The deep layers carry outlier channels ahead of the final norm: max-abs reaches 17.4 at L27 while cosine holds at 0.99992, and a max-abs threshold would report catastrophic failure on a correct port. This was predicted from the reference port before any measurement existed and the measurements have the same shape. Max-abs is recorded per probe as observed, for review rather than for gating.

The waveform gates on both. A listener hears the waveform, and a cosine over it would hide a constant offset.

Every threshold is five times the measured deviation in (1 - cosine). That headroom is wide enough to absorb run-to-run variation and far tighter than any defect this suite has caught: a transposed code stream gave cosine 0.017, and a prompt built one position short gave -0.01.

source-bf16-oracle-vs-f32-cpu.description: The oracle's codes replayed through the port on CPU, compared against its prefill probes and waveform.
